Q: Apply a user-defined function (UDF) to Pandas A:

You have made a common beginner's mistake. It has to be

if ("Coco" in x) or ('SAINSBURYS' in x):

And if you have a longer list then you can use a for-loop

def tans_cat(x):

    all_words = ['Coco', 'SAINSBURYS']

    # --- loop ---

    for word in all_words:
        if word in x:
            return 1

    # --- after loop ---

    return 0

You may also create a string like Coco|SAINSBURYS
and use the module re to check the string which you get in x

def tran_cat(x):
    all_words = ["Coco", "SAINSBURYS"]

    pattern = "|".join(all_words)

    if re.search(pattern, x):
        return 1
    else:
        return 0

If words may have characters which have special meaning in regular expressions, then you may need to use re.escape() on every word

    pattern = "|".join(re.escape(word) for word in all_words)

Full code used for test

(by the way, all versions also give 1 for Cocolino because it contains Coco, and I don't know if that is what you expect)

import pandas as pd
import re


def tran_cat_1(x):
    # if x['Desc'].str.contains('|'.join(["Coco", 'SAINSBURYS'])):
    # if ("Coco" or "SAINSBURYS") in x:
    if ("Coco" in x) or ("SAINSBURYS" in x):
        return 1
    else:
        return 0


def tran_cat_2(x):
    all_words = ["Coco", "SAINSBURYS"]

    for word in all_words:
        if word in x:
            return 1
    # --- after loop ---
    return 0


def tran_cat_3(x):
    all_words = ["Coco", "SAINSBURYS"]

    pattern = "|".join(all_words)
    print(f"{pattern=}")

    if re.search(pattern, x):
        return 1
    else:
        return 0

# --- main ---

z1 = pd.DataFrame({"Desc":
    ["A", "B", "Cocolino", "Coco", "SAINT SAINSBURYS", "C", "D"]})

z1["Tran_Cat_1"] = z1["Desc"].apply(tran_cat_1)
z1["Tran_Cat_2"] = z1["Desc"].apply(tran_cat_2)
z1["Tran_Cat_3"] = z1["Desc"].apply(tran_cat_3)

print(z1)

Q: How can I read a local text file in the browser? A:

Local Ajax calls in Chrome are not supported due to the same-origin policy

The error message in Chrome is like this:

Cross origin requests are not supported for protocol schemes: http, data, chrome, chrome-extension, https.

This means that Chrome creates a virtual disk for every domain to keep the files served by the domain using the HTTP and HTTPS protocols. Any access to files outside this virtual disk are restricted under the same-origin policy. Ajax requests and responses happen on HTTP/HTTPS. Therefore they won’t work for local files.

Firefox does not put on such a restriction, and therefore your code will work happily in the Firefox. However, there are workarounds for Chrome too.

Q: Bluetooth permissions on iOS 18 A:

UTImportedTypeDeclarations is irrelevant to Core Bluetooth.

You must append the following key element and the subsequent string element in the dict element.

    <key>NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription</key>
    <string>Your own usage description</string>

You can also see them with the key of "Privacy - Bluetooth Always Usage Description" on Xcode UI.

If the Info.plist is configured correctly, Bluetooth permission alert ("Your App" Would Like to Use Bluetooth) should be displayed when CBCentralManager (or CBPeripheralManager) is first initialized.

Q: Storing Crystal Reports in XML files? A:

There's a GitHub project that will convert RPT to XML. The tool is intended for diffs, so I don't know if there is an XML-to-RPT converter. Crystal Reports can not take the XML file and open it like a .rpt file. But if you're using Git for version control, the XML is useful to know what actually changed between each version of the .rpt

If you use Git, you can set up a pre-commit hook that will create the .xml version of the .rpt file:

.git/hooks/pre-commit

#!/bin/sh
# Find staged .rpt files and generate matching .xml files
git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.rpt$' | while read -r rpt_file; do
    xml_file="${rpt_file%.rpt}.xml"
    rpttoxml "$rpt_file" "$xml_file"
    git add "$xml_file"
done

This tool is also useful if you don't have a login to the database server, but you need to get the SQL or other details about the report.

Q: How to create new local branch and switch between branches in Git A:

Since Git v2.23, the git switch command has been added as an alternative to git checkout. Subjectively, the syntax is more idiomatic.

git switch --create NEW_BRANCH_NAME

# Short form
git switch -c NEW_BRANCH_NAME
